clue.text: Shared an understanding with shyest maid, trembling, keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the shuffled letters wrap round the next piece
trembling suggests shaking and disorder, so the letters of shyest maid are rearranged

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A sympathetic listener comforts a nervous, shaking maid who keeps silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' rearranges SHYEST MAID, and 'keeping' puts P (quiet) inside that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sympathise is to share someone's feelings and understand their position, so past tense matches.

clue.text: Before start of December fir gets nicely dressed

indicators.note: before places the tree's name ahead of the following letter

parts.note: the spruce is a fir-like conifer

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of December is used

explanation.surface: A Christmas tree is decorated nicely just before December begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruced, as in spruced up, means smartened or neatly turned out.

clue.text: Edmund early in the morning upset lass

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edmund
one a.m., written I AM with I for one, is an early hour

explanation.surface: Edmund is disturbed in the early hours by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NED + IAM upside down; 'early in the morning' is 1 a.m., written I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an old word for a girl or young unmarried woman.

clue.text: A story about company that may be ratified

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story wraps round the business

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A tale about a business that might get official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affirmable can be confirmed or upheld, as a ratified decision is.

clue.text: Keep secret identity when entertained by the fellow

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being held as a guest within, so ID goes inside

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male, the fellow
ID is the short form of identity, as in an ID card

explanation.surface: A man conceals who he is while playing host.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to conceal it, keeping it from others.

clue.text: With blemishes all around, America suffers

indicators.note: all around means the marks surround the country's abbreviation

parts.note: stains are marks or blemishes
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: America endures, its reputation stained on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an injury or loss is to suffer it; both verbs mean undergo.

clue.text: SS and similar folk

definitions.meaning: two S letters side by side form a doubled letter

explanation.surface: The Nazi SS and people of a similar sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubles are pairs of repeated letters and also people who look exactly like others.

clue.text: City oddball, one with two females in tow

indicators.note: in tow means following behind, so the females come after the other pieces

parts.note: a card is an informal word for an eccentric or comic person
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the standard abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: An eccentric townsman goes about with two women trailing after him.
explanation.walkthrough: CARD is a colloquial word for a quirky person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: One goes round very quickly and one's teeth are on edge

definitions.text: One goes round very quickly and one's teeth are on edge

parts.words: One goes round very quickly and one's teeth are on edge
parts.note: reads like a nervous person rushing about, but describes a spinning toothed blade whose teeth sit on its rim

explanation.surface: Someone dashing around in a state of jittery nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teeth on edge' means anxious, but here it is literal: the teeth line the blade's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular saw is a power tool with a toothed disc blade that spins at high speed.

clue.text: Upset daughter is the opposite of sweet, rolling over

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

indicators.note: rolling over means turning round, so the word for dry wine is read backwards

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne, the opposite of sweet

explanation.surface: A girl is distressed that her sweet nature has turned sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs meaning to agitate or discompose someone emotionally.

clue.text: Club against money demanded for police action

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall
a charge is a price asked for something

explanation.surface: A club is up in arms over fees it must pay for policing.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton charge is a rush by police wielding truncheons to disperse a crowd.

clue.text: Form of technology — something hard engineers initially attempt

parts.note: rock is a typical example of something hard

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of engineers is used

parts.note: to try is to attempt something

explanation.surface: Engineers begin a hard new attempt at some branch of technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and engineering of rockets, a branch of technology.

clue.text: Play in small country community

definitions.meaning: a Shakespeare tragedy about a Danish prince
a village too small to have its own church

explanation.surface: A play set in a small rural village.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Shakespeare's tragedy and a tiny rural settlement.

clue.text: Famous Argentinian side lifted cup — what gets those gnashers going?

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, was born in Argentina
a wing is a side of a building or a team

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised up, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mug is a drinking cup

explanation.surface: A famous Argentine team lift the trophy, a sight to make fans grind their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns MUG into GUM; gnashers is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing gum keeps the jaws and teeth working as it is chewed.

clue.text: Language used by loud Russians in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Noisy Russians are falling back, shouting in some language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, widely spoken in India too.

clue.text: Come by to fight or bless?

definitions.meaning: to come by something is to obtain or get hold of it
to attack or assault someone physically
the laying on of hands is a rite of blessing or healing

explanation.surface: A question about whether a visitor drops in to brawl or to give a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to seize or obtain, to assault, and to touch someone in blessing.

clue.text: A darn cig ruined jacket

indicators.note: ruined suggests wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wretched cigarette has burnt a hole in someone's jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket that buttons down the front.

clue.text: Day of celebration with everyone needing permits to go round hospital

indicators.note: to go round means to encircle, so the joined words enclose the next letter
needing joins the two words side by side, one followed by the other

parts.note: all means everyone
to allow is to permit, so permits gives the verb form
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A festival where everyone needs a pass to tour the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' wraps the joined pair around the hospital letter, so it lands where the two words meet.
explanation.definitionFit: All Hallows is All Saints' Day, 1 November, a feast day in the Christian calendar.

clue.text: Man on board goes down after short jump — when the vessel's this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going down after means placed below, so the chess piece follows
short means cut off, so the last letter of the word for jump is dropped

parts.note: to leap is to jump
the king is a piece, or man, on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A sailor jumps and sinks, asking what state the ship must be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a sailor but is a chess piece; 'short' trims LEAP to LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that is letting water in is leaking, and so may go down.

clue.text: That's contemptible, having Greek character shut up

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sh is the sound made to tell someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a Greek fellow who's been told to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pish is an old exclamation of scorn or impatience, like 'pah' or 'nonsense'.

clue.text: Huge fellows squeezed into semi, getting sozzled

indicators.note: squeezed into means pushed inside, so the men go within the shuffled letters
sozzled means drunk, suggesting the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: Lots of men cram into a semi-detached house and get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house; 'getting sozzled' gives IMSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is a synonym of huge, meaning extremely large.

clue.text: Locks to secure old books? That's silly talk!

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast within, so the locks enclose the books' abbreviation

parts.note: locks are strands of hair
OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Using locks to keep old books safe is nonsense, someone scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is an idiom for empty, boastful or nonsensical talk.

clue.text: Puts up with spectators' accommodation

definitions.meaning: the tiered seating areas at a sports ground

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the seating provided for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for tolerating and a noun for grandstands at a stadium.

clue.text: One telling tales in class with little hesitation

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A schoolchild sneaks on classmates, barely hesitating to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a school class or year group in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer passes on secret or damaging information about others, a telltale.

clue.text: Fast runner heading off over a field

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the next piece
heading off means the head, or first letter, is removed

parts.note: the hare is a famously fast animal

explanation.surface: A speedy animal dashes off across a field.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a field of study or activity, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Footballer around half-time's first person to grumble

indicators.note: around means the player's name surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a winger is a footballer who plays on the flank

indicators.note: first means taking only the opening letter of half-time

explanation.surface: A footballer moans to his team-mates around the half-time break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts H, the first letter of 'half-time', inside WINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinger is someone who complains constantly and peevishly, a moaner.

clue.text: Greek lady that is one of a senior generation

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name, a typical crossword lady
ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A Greek woman, that is, one of the older generation.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother belongs to the generation two steps above her grandchildren.

clue.text: Greedier man troubled officers abroad

indicators.note: troubled suggests stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A greedy official makes trouble for police officers overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The gendarmerie is the French armed police force, so foreign officers.
